answer: An agent market selling meadow surveys and yarrow crop forecasts can weight votes on shared spending by deposited collateral, locked for a fixed time horizon. Each unit of collateral buys one unit of voting power, regardless of how many identities hold it. Splitting a deposit among a thousand fake agents therefore adds no influence. To capture a majority, an attacker must lock more collateral than all honest voters combined, tying up that capital for the full period.
